objective: Find why the Claude desktop app (Windows, Code tab on this WSL checkout) lists holyagent as a user-added marketplace plugin and shows no plugin installed by the project, and what install records are duplicated.
scope: Project side: /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent/.claude/settings.json (extraKnownMarketplaces.holyagent directory path ".", enabledPlugins holyagent@holyagent) and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (source ./packages/integrations/claude/dist, version 0.1.1-2).

WSL side: /home/davidbasile/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json, installed_plugins.json, the cache folder /home/davidbasile/.claude/plugins/cache/holyagent, /home/davidbasile/.claude/settings.json enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces, /home/davidbasile/.claude.json project entries for this path.

Windows side: the same files under /mnt/c/Users/*/.claude/ (plugins/*.json, settings.json, cache) and the desktop app data under /mnt/c/Users/*/AppData/Roaming/Claude/ (config and any claude-code settings or logs mentioning holyagent or plugins).

Report every record of a holyagent install or marketplace (file, scope, path, version, gitCommitSha), which records the desktop app reads (WSL or Windows home), and the likely reason the project install is not recognized (path mismatch, scope, trust, settings shape). Say which records are duplicates and which single install should remain.
constraints: Read-only. Do not edit anything or touch .git or .holyagent.
Do not copy tokens, keys, cookies or other credentials into the report; name the file and field instead.

criteria.text: Every holyagent marketplace and install record found on the WSL and Windows sides is listed with file, scope, path and version.
The reason the desktop app does not show a project install is stated with evidence, or marked Unknown with what was searched.
The duplicate records to remove and the one install to keep are named.

result:
result: The desktop app's "user-added marketplace plugin" is a separate account-level remote plugin record that is not the project install. The project install exists only in WSL files, and the desktop app does not read them for its plugin list. Cause is partly inferred (see Likely reason).

## Likely reason the project install is not recognized
- Confirmed: the desktop app's plugin list reads its own remote plugin manager store (AppData/Roaming/Claude/rpm, an account and organization sync of a marketplace_... entry). Its record says user-added and "available", not installed by a project. It has no projectPath, so it cannot be matched to the project install.
- Confirmed: the project install (scope project, projectPath /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent) lives only in the WSL home's installed_plugins.json. The Windows home has no installed_plugins.json and no holyagent marketplace. The desktop Code tab keys the project as "wsl:ubuntu:/home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent", while the WSL CLI keys it as the plain path.
- Confirmed: the WSL install works. It is trusted, usageCount is 141, and the dependencies are installed.
- Unknown: I could not read the desktop app's code, so I did not verify that it ignores the WSL installed_plugins.json for display. The cause is inferred from the files above. I found no log line that says why the project install is hidden.
- Not the cause: the path, version, trust and settings shape are all consistent in WSL. The directory marketplace path "." resolves to the same path that known_marketplaces.json records. Both plugin.json files say 0.1.1-2.
- Hypothesis: the Windows-side holyagent copy is a manual or desktop "add marketplace" upload (installedBy user). It is an independent record and lists the plugin as available. It is not a duplicate of the project install in a form the app would merge.

## Duplicates and what to keep
Duplicates:
- The scope user entries for billion-context@billion-context and exa@claude-plugins-official in installed_plugins.json. They duplicate the scope project entries, which have auto:true and the same installPath, version and sha. The scope user entries were installed at 13:47:41Z.
- The Windows-app copy of holyagent (rpm manifest entry plugin_01WLushN2uAXQKokkx6ju19v and its folder). It duplicates the WSL holyagent@holyagent project install.
- The marketplace "holyagent" is declared in two places: the project settings.json (directory ".") and WSL known_marketplaces.json (absolute path). That pair is normal. The project settings.json entry is the source of truth.

Keep:
- The single holyagent@holyagent entry in WSL installed_plugins.json with scope project and projectPath /home/davidbasile/dev/holyagent, version 0.1.1-2, sha ba1bb8de.... Keep the project .claude/settings.json enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces entries that drive it.
- Keep one of the two dependency installs. The project-scope entries are auto-managed, so remove the scope user ones if you want a single install of each. Removing the user scope also needs the user-level enabledPlugins entries in /home/davidbasile/.claude/settings.json to be checked, since those enable the same two plugins.

## Removal actions for the root or user (I made no edits)
- Remove or uninstall the user-added holyagent marketplace plugin from the desktop app's plugin UI, which clears the rpm manifest entry.
- Remove the user-scope duplicate entries via the claude plugin CLI.
